message.content:
**Answer:** The sculpture that is often cited as the most iconic and widely recognized work of the 19th‑century is **“The Kiss” by Auguste Rodin** (1889). It captures the emotional intensity and realism that defined much of late‑Victorian sculpture and remains one of the most reproduced and celebrated pieces from that era. --- ### Why “The Kiss”? | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin (1840–1917) | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist; early modernism | | **Subject** | A passionate embrace between two lovers | | **Impact** | • Became a symbol of Romantic love and human intimacy.
• Influenced subsequent generations of sculptors.
• Widely reproduced in bronze, marble, and other media. | | **Legacy** | • Displayed in major museums worldwide (e.g., Musée Rodin, Paris; National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.).
• Continues to inspire contemporary artists and popular culture. | --- ### Contextual Comparison | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Significance | |-----------|--------|------|--------------| | **“The Kiss”** | Rodin | 1889 | Most reproduced 19th‑century sculpture; epitomizes late‑Victorian romanticism. | | **“The Gates of Hell”** | Rodin | 1880–1917 | Massive monumental work; showcases Rodin’s mastery of complex composition. | | **“The Thinker”** | Rodin | 1902 (first cast) | Iconic figure of modern thought; technically a 20th‑century masterpiece, though conceived in the 19th. | | **“The Birth of Venus”** (original) | Botticelli | 1484–1486 | Renaissance classic; not a 19th‑century creation. | --- ### Quick Takeaway - **Most famous 19th‑century sculpture:** *“The Kiss”* (Rodin, 1889). - **Why it stands out:** Its universal theme, technical innovation, and enduring popularity make it the quintessential representation of 19th‑century sculpture.
